sections.h2: Where is the Cochise County Recorder and when is it open?
sections.html:
The Recorder's office is at 1415 Melody Lane, Building B, in Bisbee, Arizona 85603. It is open Monday through Friday, 8 am to 5 pm, according to the county's Recorder page.

The office does two jobs: it processes documents tied to real estate transactions, and it keeps voter registration records for the county. Sellers deal with the first job.

sections.h2: What sort of county is Cochise County?
sections.html:
Cochise County covers 6,219 square miles in the southeastern corner of Arizona and borders Mexico on its south side. Wikipedia lists it as close in size to Rhode Island and Connecticut combined, with a 2020 population of 125,447.

The county was founded February 1, 1881. Bisbee is the county seat, and the courthouse there is an art deco building. Sierra Vista is the largest city. The county neighbors Santa Cruz, Pima, Graham and Greenlee counties in Arizona and Hidalgo County in New Mexico.

Protected land is a big part of the map. The county holds Chiricahua National Park, Coronado National Memorial, Fort Bowie National Historic Site, Kartchner Caverns State Park and part of Coronado National Forest. Because the county is so large, a seller should phone ahead before driving to the Recorder in Bisbee.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Cochise County?
sections.html:
Recording any document costs $30, and the county says this is a flat fee as of July 1, 2019 under A.R.S. 11-475. Government agencies pay $15.

Record any document$30

Military discharge (A.R.S. 11-465)No charge
Copies, per page$1
Certification of a copy, per document$3
Mail or email processing fee$1

The fee page lists no separate county transfer tax line. Ask the office or your title company about any charge not shown there.

sections.h2: What is the affidavit of real property value, and who needs it?
sections.html:
Every property sale needs a completed affidavit of real property value or an exemption number, and the Recorder will refuse the deed without one. The county's FAQ says all sale transactions require it, and it points questions to the Arizona Department of Revenue at 602-716-6843.

The statute behind it is A.R.S. 11-1133. Seller and buyer jointly certify details such as names and mailing addresses, a tax statement address, the legal description, the date of sale, total consideration and financing type, the assessor's parcel number, and whether the home will be owner-occupied or rented. Section 11-1134 lists the exemptions, and the instrument has to carry a note of the exemption claimed.

Examples of exempt transfers include a deed of gift, a deed made under court order, and a nominal-consideration transfer between spouses, parents and children, grandparents and grandchildren, or siblings. A sale for delinquent taxes is also listed.

sections.h2: What happens to a deed after it reaches the Recorder?
sections.html:
If the document meets form requirements, is complete and carries the right fee, the office accepts it and makes it permanent public record. The county describes the steps in its FAQ:

  1. The data entry department keys the key details to build an index.
  2. The microfilm department films and optically scans the document.
  3. The original is returned to the address typed on the document.
  4. A certified copy can be ordered later if the original is lost.

The county says to allow 15 to 20 business days for documents to come back. That is worth knowing if you are mailing a deed and want the original in hand. Your title or escrow company often handles the recording for a sale, so ask them before you plan a trip.

sections.h2: How do I get a copy of a deed or a plat from the Recorder?
sections.html:
You can request a copy of a deed in person or by mail at the Bisbee address, at $1 a page, or $2 a page if it is faxed. A copy of a survey or plat map costs $5.00 a page when you give the book and page of the map, according to the county FAQ.

The fee page adds that a certification costs $3 per document and that copies of maps are $3 at 11 by 17 inches and $1 at 8 1/2 by 11 inches. Recording a map sheet costs $24 for the first sheet and $20 for each additional sheet, with lower rates for government agencies.

sections.h2: Who do I contact for a recording question?
sections.html:
Call 520-432-8350 or the toll free line at 888-457-4513 during office hours, or email through the link on the Recorder page. The county says forms for recording are available at most office supply or stationery stores, so the office does not hand them out.

For a homestead question, the FAQ points to A.R.S. 33-1101 and an attorney. For a business name, it points to A.R.S. 44-1236 and the Arizona statutes on entities. The Recorder describes what it records, but it does not offer legal advice on how to title your house.

sections.h2: Can the Recorder tell me about liens, owners and foreclosures?
sections.html:
Partly. Records at the office are found by searching a grantor and grantee name index, and you can run your own title search in person or hire a title company. The county's FAQ says it cannot tell you the owner by parcel number, which is a job for the Assessor at 520-432-8650.

Other answers from the FAQ:

  • To see liens on a property, search the index in the office or ask a title company.
  • To learn a selling price, come in and look for a recorded affidavit of real property value.
  • To research a foreclosure, get the owner's name or street address and visit the office.
  • For adding or removing a name, using a trust or removing a decedent from a deed, the county points people to a title company or an attorney.

A copy of a deed costs $1 a page, or $2 a page by fax.

sections.h2: How does recording tie into selling an inherited or tax-delinquent Cochise house?
sections.html:
Recording is the last public step in a sale, and several documents may reach this office along the way. A beneficiary deed must be recorded before the owner's death to work under A.R.S. 33-405. An affidavit of succession for a small estate is recorded here after the court registrar issues a certified copy (A.R.S. 14-3971). A certificate of redemption after a tax lien sale may be recorded here too (A.R.S. 42-18154).

If your Cochise County house has one of those issues, gather the recorded paperwork first. A title company can then tell you what must be cleared before a deed to a buyer can be recorded.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in Cochise County?
faqs.a: Record it at the Cochise County Recorder, 1415 Melody Lane, Building B, Bisbee, AZ 85603. The office is open Monday to Friday, 8 am to 5 pm, and the phone is 520-432-8350.

faqs.q: How much does the Cochise County Recorder charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: The fee is a flat $30 per document, or $15 for government agencies, under A.R.S. 11-475. Copies are $1 a page and certification is $3.

faqs.q: How long does it take to get my recorded documents back?
faqs.a: The county says to expect 15 to 20 business days. The original returns to the address typed on the document.

faqs.q: What does the Recorder say about adding or removing a name from a deed?
faqs.a: The county FAQ says to consult a title company or an attorney. The same answer applies to moving property into or out of a trust and to removing a decedent's name from a deed.

faqs.q: Do I need an affidavit of real property value to record a sale deed?
faqs.a: Yes, unless an exemption applies. The Recorder requires a completed affidavit or an exemption number on every sale, and the Arizona Department of Revenue can answer form questions.

faqs.q: Can the Recorder tell me who owns a parcel?
faqs.a: No. The county refers owner-by-parcel questions to the Assessor at 520-432-8650. The Recorder searches by grantor and grantee name.
